role: Supervises native game-server instances in their own cgroups, holds desired state, and does crash-restart and boot autostart.

fields.label: Log level
fields.description: Minimum severity this leaf logs.

fields.label: KGSM executable
fields.description: Path to the KGSM executable. Required: the watchdog reads each instance's spawn configuration through it before forking the game, so it has nothing to supervise without one.

fields.label: Instances directory
fields.description: KGSM's instances directory, watched for the per-instance event channels that drive player presence and container lifecycle. Empty derives it under the KGSM user's data directory; set it only to relocate it.

fields.label: Control socket
fields.description: Unix socket the watchdog serves its control plane on. Every surface that starts or stops a native server reaches it here.

fields.label: Control socket permissions
fields.description: Octal permission bits applied to the control socket. These are the whole security boundary — the socket can start and kill game servers, and the daemon does no authentication of its own.

fields.label: Cgroup v2 mount point
fields.description: Where the cgroup v2 hierarchy is mounted. Everything the watchdog supervises lives below this path.

fields.label: Cgroup base (fallback)
fields.description: Fallback name for KGSM's delegated cgroup base. The real base is discovered from the daemon's own cgroup, so this is used only when that discovery finds nothing.

fields.label: Cgroup controllers
fields.description: Controllers enabled on the base subtree so each per-instance cgroup inherits them. Dropping one removes the matching per-server metric.

fields.label: Supervisor leaf cgroup
fields.description: Name of the cgroup the daemon itself sits in, a sibling of every instance cgroup. It has to be a leaf, because cgroup v2 forbids enabling controllers on a cgroup that holds processes.

fields.label: Supervision poll interval
fields.description: How often each supervised instance is checked for liveness. This bounds how quickly a crash is noticed.

fields.label: Restart policy
fields.description: What counts as restartable. 'always' restarts any exit while the instance is meant to be running; 'on-failure' leaves a clean exit stopped. Many games exit 0 on a crash, which is why 'always' is the default.

fields.label: First restart delay
fields.description: How long to wait before the first restart attempt. The delay doubles with each consecutive failure.

fields.label: Maximum restart delay
fields.description: Ceiling on the doubling restart delay, so a long failure streak still retries at a predictable rate.

fields.label: Maximum consecutive restarts
fields.description: How many consecutive failures to tolerate before giving up on an instance and marking it failed. Zero means never restart.

fields.label: Stability window
fields.description: How long an instance must stay up before it counts as healthy and its failure streak resets.

fields.label: Maximum park duration
fields.description: How long a server may stay parked for maintenance before the watchdog brings it back on its own. A leaf parks a server to do disruptive work against it and releases the park when the work is done; this is the deadline that applies when the leaf never gets that far, so a crashed scheduler costs a maintenance window instead of leaving a server down.

fields.label: Post-spawn grace period
fields.description: How long after spawning an instance crash detection stays suppressed, so a slow-starting game is not mistaken for a crash.

fields.label: Desired-state file
fields.description: File holding the set of instances that should come back up after a restart or reboot. Empty derives it under the KGSM user's data directory. Pointing it elsewhere orphans the existing set, and those instances stop being started at boot.

fields.label: Player presence poll interval
fields.description: How often the player-presence channels are scanned and tailed. This bounds how quickly a join or leave is reported.

fields.label: Container lifecycle poll interval
fields.description: How often a container's self-reported lifecycle channel is scanned and tailed. This drives port forwarding open and closed as a container starts and stops.

fields.label: Console follow interval
fields.description: How often a followed console polls a native instance's log for new lines. Tighter than the other pollers because someone is watching the output live.

fields.label: Firewall socket
fields.description: Control socket of the kgsm-firewall authority, which the supervisor asks to open an instance's ports when it starts and to close them when it stops. An unreachable authority is logged and never blocks a start.

fields.label: Router forward check interval
fields.description: How often to check that the router still holds the port forwards your running servers need, and restore any it dropped. A router can accept a forward, call the lease permanent, and discard it anyway — leaving a server running but unreachable from the internet with nothing to announce it. This interval is how long that can go unnoticed. Set to 0 to stop checking.
